# Daniel 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue ninety feet tall and nine feet wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

**2** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**3** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**4** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**9** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**10** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**11** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**12** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**13** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**14** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**15** A herald shouted, 'People of all races, nations, and languages — when you hear the music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue!'

**16** Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied, "O Nebuchadnezzar, we don't need to defend ourselves before you.

**17** If we are thrown into the blazing furnace, the God we serve is able to deliver us from it, and He will rescue us from your hand, Your Majesty.

**18** But even if He doesn't, we want you to know, Your Majesty, that we will never serve your gods or worship the gold statue you have set up."

**19** Nebuchadnezzar was so furious with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego that his face was distorted with rage. He commanded that the furnace be heated seven times hotter than usual.

**20** The soldiers tied them up and threw them into the roaring furnace.

**21** The soldiers tied them up and threw them into the roaring furnace.

**22** The soldiers tied them up and threw them into the roaring furnace.

**23** The soldiers tied them up and threw them into the roaring furnace.

**24** But suddenly, Nebuchadnezzar jumped to his feet in amazement and exclaimed to his advisers, "Didn't we throw three men into the fire, all tied up?" "Yes, Your Majesty," they replied.

**25** "Look!" he answered. "I see four men walking around in the fire, completely unharmed! And the fourth looks like a divine being!"

**26** Then Nebuchadnezzar went as close as he could to the door of the flaming furnace and shouted: "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!" So they stepped out of the fire.

**27** Then the highest officials of the kingdom crowded around them and saw that the fire had not touched them. Not a hair on their heads was singed, their robes were not scorched, and they didn't even smell like smoke!

**28** Then Nebuchadnezzar said, "Praise to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego! He sent His angel to rescue His servants who trusted in Him. They defied the king's command and were willing to die rather than serve or worship any god except their own God."

**29** Therefore, I decree that if any people of any race, nation, or language speak against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, they will be torn limb from limb and their houses demolished. For there is no other god who can rescue like this!

**30** Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in the province of Babylon.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:17-18**: "But even if He doesn't" — these five words are the backbone of biblical faith. God CAN save. We believe He WILL. But even if He DOESN'T, we're not changing our answer. That's what real faith looks like.

- **3:25**: A fourth figure appears in the fire — and even the pagan king recognizes something divine. The furnace doesn't just fail to destroy them; it becomes a place of encounter.

- **3:27**: They didn't even smell like smoke. When God delivers, He doesn't do half-measures. Not singed, not scorched, not even the smell of what should have killed them.

— PNEUMA
